Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear list. Short answer: Redwood does not use customer content from hosted or private deployments to train public or internal models as part of our standard product offering. That includes production request payloads, customer documents, and transcripts.

I'll attach the formal attestation and our SOC 2 summary; Mina (Security) and Marissa (Legal) are looped in for the operational and contractual details below. High-level points:

- Warranty statement (for contract): 
  • "Redwood Inference warrants that customer-provided content, including request payloads, files, and transcripts, will not be used to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve Redwood models, unless explicitly agreed in writing."

- Backups / snapshots / logs:
  • We keep short-lived operational logs for debugging and billing; those logs are retained for 30 days by default and are not used for model training.
  • Customer snapshots (backups) created for customer-managed Private deployments follow the customer's storage policies; Redwood does not ingest Private deployment backups into any model training pipelines.
  • For Hosted deployments, longer-term archives (rare, e.g., legal holds) are stored encrypted and access-controlled; they are not part of any training corpus.

- Debugging traces & ephemeral caches:
  • Transient KV caches and live inference traces used for troubleshooting are treated as ephemeral; debug snapshots are only retained for short windows (configurable, typically 7–30 days) and are excluded from training processes.

- Signed attestation & next steps:
  • Attached: draft attestation template and SOC summary. If FinTrust needs a countersigned attestation on your paper, we can route a DocuSign.

I'll let Mina add the operational retention specifics and Marissa confirm contract language.

Hi all — quick operational clarifications from Security: 

1) Logs and telemetry: application-level telemetry (metrics, aggregated traces) is used for product improvement when it is aggregated and deidentified. Raw request payloads are never included.

2) Snapshots & backups: for Hosted customers we retain encrypted snapshots for up to 180 days for recovery; these are stored in a segregated bucket per-customer. Access is restricted to a subset of on-call engineers and governed by IAM policies and audit logs. Those snapshots are NOT fed into training pipelines.

3) Legal holds & eDiscovery: if FinTrust issues a legal hold, we will retain the specified data and can provide export; legal hold data remains segregated and is not used for any operational modeling.

4) Exceptional incident investigation: in rare incidents (security breach, active forensics) a copy of relevant content may be staged for internal investigation; such copies are time-boxed, access-controlled, and explicitly excluded from training — and we will notify customers when that occurs per our incident policy.

Operational knobs you might want to set:
- Archive TTL: we can set shorter retention for your tenant (e.g., 30/90/180 days).
- Debug snapshot window: default 14 days; we can reduce to 7 for customers with strict requirements.

If you are comfortable with the warranty language Naomi suggested, Marissa can embed it into the SOW and we can push a countersign via DocuSign.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
